title: Agentic Software Engineering: Build, Verify, Evaluate
overview: English is the first teaching language. Learn to enter an unfamiliar repository, clarify a requirement, use an agent for a bounded task and decide whether the evidence supports the change.

Use the navigation to read the syllabus, complete Week 0 setup and follow the weekly route. The teacher's CI dashboard case grows from a status error into a reviewed, evaluated and operated product. Each student works in their own copy of the `ci-dashboard` repository and delivers one complete feature.

The course has fourteen weeks, three personal practices and five project workshops. Reuse your work: the individual checks and defense contribute 40 points, the individual project 45 and P1/P2/P3 contribute 15. You pass with at least 60 overall and 20/40 on the independent components. The syllabus explains feedback, equivalent resits and evidence reuse.

Each week has a published hour estimate that includes setup, waiting, collaboration, practice and revision; it is planning guidance, not a cap. Ask for help at the published checkpoints; optional features and extra tool integrations are not prerequisites for full marks.

weeks.topic: A plausible patch and a failing build
weeks.lecture: Inspect a dashboard status error; predict a counterexample; explain context, generation and tool execution.
weeks.workshop: Start P1 with four contrasting first attempts and one saved prediction.

weeks.topic: Build and inspect a small agent
weeks.lecture: Trace request validation, tool effects, observations and stopping in a small controller.
weeks.workshop: Finish P1 with a bounded read/write/bash loop and five controller tasks.

weeks.topic: Find the change in an unfamiliar repository
weeks.lecture: Trace one dashboard request across files; select context and a bounded edit; compare two context packets.
weeks.workshop: Map a ci-dashboard call path, compare fixed-budget contexts, check one permission boundary, use one standard skill on ci-dashboard and carry it read-only to an unfamiliar permissively licensed open-source repository.

weeks.topic: Turn a user need into an executable specification
weeks.lecture: Separate observations from assumptions; decide a feature boundary and independent acceptance cases.
weeks.workshop: Run two discovery activities of your own for M0 and one feature specification.

weeks.topic: Deliver a small change without breaking callers
weeks.lecture: Protect existing behavior, inspect dependencies and complete an explainable first PR.
weeks.workshop: Start M1; CP1 is a 30-minute individual diagnosis, test and repair after practice.

weeks.topic: Review and delegate a bounded change
weeks.lecture: Compare a specification, human findings and agent findings; decide ownership and integration checks.
weeks.workshop: P2: review one short change against its acceptance criteria before reading any supplied or agent review, reproduce a finding or support a no-finding with the inputs checked, and revise after feedback.

weeks.lecture: Use a surviving mutant to select a property and a reproducible fuzz input.
weeks.workshop: Strengthen the same M1 tests and explain a regression that previously escaped.

weeks.topic: Protect the agent and the application
weeks.lecture: Distinguish data from authority; reproduce an inert attack; verify permitted work still succeeds.
weeks.workshop: Repair one local attack chain, run supplied regressions and close M1 security issues.

weeks.topic: Compare workflows with a fixed experiment
weeks.lecture: Freeze task identity and budgets; separate success, timeout, repair and missing evidence.
weeks.workshop: P3: audit four original synthetic tasks and three traces; compare one real run with another verified record.

weeks.topic: Test the evaluator and build a regression gate
weeks.lecture: Write the evaluation contract; challenge a code scorer and calibrate a model judge.
weeks.workshop: Build the project evaluator for M2; obtain feedback and revise before freezing.

weeks.topic: Recover a user path after an incident
weeks.lecture: CP2: 30-minute individual unfamiliar-code review and recovery reasoning; then examine logs, retries and idempotency.
weeks.workshop: Use the supplied local drill on M2; prove recovery and begin scheduled user testing.

weeks.topic: Verify a model audit with reproducible evidence
weeks.lecture: Freeze one feature and distinguish a demonstrated defect from an untested suspicion.
weeks.workshop: M3: receive the teaching team's model audit of a frozen snapshot of your repository, then reproduce, refute or bound each evaluation, security and maintenance finding and add one check of your own.
weeks.deliverables: M3 verified audit; continue user testing

weeks.topic: Respond to findings and improve usability
weeks.lecture: Disposition an audit item; observe a neutral user task and verify the resulting interface change.
weeks.workshop: Complete the three user tests begun in week 11; repair and regress; begin individual defense.
weeks.deliverables: M4 repair response; user tests; individual defense

weeks.lecture: Connect a user need, a change and its evidence; answer a new variation independently.
weeks.workshop: M4: expo-style demonstration with staff and peer questions; finish individually scheduled defenses.
weeks.deliverables: M4 release artifact; individual defense; final calibration
